n.story:
Your role is transitioning from a high-speed manual sorter to a specialized animal welfare and biosecurity technician. While the core task of determining the sex of a chick is being rapidly automated by high-speed computer vision systems and genetic markers, your physical presence remains indispensable. AI cannot replicate the delicate dexterity required to handle live, unpredictable animals without causing distress, nor can it replace the human 'gut feeling' for animal health that comes from years of physical interaction.

As AI takes over the repetitive visual identification, you will find yourself spending more time managing the environment and health of the flock. You will use AI-driven dashboards to monitor epidemiological patterns and biosecurity risks in real-time, shifting your focus from individual sorting to the holistic oversight of the facility. Your value will lie in your ability to interpret complex animal welfare regulations and ensure that automated systems are operating ethically and safely.
